title: Body Sealants, Adhesives and Lubricant
introduction:
I use this table to match a body-repair material to its listed product identification and specification. Read across each row: the Name column identifies the material and any listed products, while the Specification column carries the associated material requirement. Keep the separate adhesive rows separate, and treat a dash as an unprovided specification rather than permission to choose anything handy.

Seam sealer closes body-panel joints, weatherstrip seals moving openings, and adhesives and lubricants have different jobs. The tubes may look like cousins on the shelf, but they are not a universal repair kit. This table identifies materials; it does not assign every product to a repair location or establish preparation, application, cure time or interchangeability. Choose the material through the applicable body-repair procedure before applying it.

edits.why: Read the material name, product identification and specification as a connected row. A shared generic name such as Adhesive does not make separate specification entries interchangeable. The matching repair procedure supplies the location and application requirements that this materials reference cannot determine.
